summary: Simple PyTorch implementations of the Vision Transformer and dozens of its variants, ready to drop into image models.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: vit-pytorch implements the Vision Transformer (ViT), which classifies images by splitting them into patches and running a transformer over them, in a small PyTorch package. Beyond the base model it includes many variants from research papers, such as Simple ViT, NaViT, CaiT, CrossViT, MobileViT, MaxViT, 3D ViT and ViViT, plus training approaches like distillation, masked autoencoders and Dino.
sixtySeconds.problem: Vision transformer papers are hard to reproduce from scratch. This package gives clean, ready-to-use implementations of many of them in one place.
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Pick it for a quick, readable way to try ViT and its variants in PyTorch.

overview: Create a ViT with settings like image_size, patch_size, num_classes, dim, depth, heads and mlp_dim, then pass an image tensor to get predictions.
Other variants are imported the same way from vit_pytorch. It is MIT licensed.

steps.title: Import
steps.body: import torch and from vit_pytorch import ViT.

steps.title: Create the model
steps.body: ViT(image_size=256, patch_size=32, num_classes=1000, dim=1024, depth=6, heads=16, mlp_dim=2048, dropout=0.1, emb_dropout=0.1). image_size must be divisible by patch_size.

steps.title: Predict
steps.body: img = torch.randn(1, 3, 256, 256); preds = v(img) gives a (1, 1000) output.
